title: An Execution‑Oriented Evaluation of Generate→Validate→Simulate→Rollback Pipelines for LLM‑Assisted NetOps: a Confirmatory Study with gpt‑5‑mini
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory comparison of (A) a generation‑only pipeline and (C) a generate→validate→simulate→rollback (guarded) pipeline for LLM‑assisted NetOps configuration tasks (preregistration id: c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1). Under the frozen plan we ran gpt‑5‑mini on N=160 vendor‑neutral tasks (routing/ACL/NAT). A deterministic simulator adjudicated an actionable‑misconfiguration binary per task. Results (artifact‑backed): baseline actionable = 0/160; guarded actionable = 0/160; paired difference = 0.00; bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) [0.00,0.00]; McNemar exact p = 1.00. The preregistered target (≥30% relative reduction) is not evaluable because the baseline actionable rate was zero (ceiling effect). We (1) archive full preregistration, provider call logs, per‑task scoring JSONs, and analysis artifacts (SHA‑256 hashes recorded in the execution manifest), (2) describe the simulator‑scoring linkage and execution semantics, and (3) discuss construct/externally‑valid limitations and concrete recommendations for harder confirmatory sets and multi‑model follow‑ups.

sections.introduction: Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) promise to accelerate NetOps tasks (intent→configuration, change planning, limited self‑healing), but fluent model proposals can be operationally risky when enacted without robust pre‑enactment assurance [VeriFlow 2012; MeshAgent 2025; OpsEval/LogEval families]. Research gap. Prior work shows that combining generation with constraint checking or local verification can reduce obvious syntactic and semantic mistakes, yet a reproducible, preregistered, execution‑oriented comparison that links LLM generation to deterministic enactment outcomes is rare. Research question and contributions. We preregistered c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1 and asked whether a generate→validate→simulate→rollback (guarded) pipeline (C) reduces the actionable‑misconfiguration rate by ≥30% relative to a generation‑only baseline (A) on a representative vendor‑neutral task set. Contributions: (i) a fully preregistered paired confirmatory execution using gpt‑5‑mini with transparent artifacts and SHA‑256 hashes; (ii) deterministic simulator adjudication and an archived scoring record for each task; (iii) honest reporting of a ceiling effect and prescriptive guidance for future, harder benchmarks.
sections.related_work: Network verification and update checking. VeriFlow introduced dynamic invariant checking to catch configuration errors at rule insertion time [Khurshid et al., Sigcomm 2012]. Later work extended fast and incremental verifiers for reachability and policy invariants. LLM→NetOps generation plus verification. Verified Prompt Programming (router config translation), MeshAgent (constraint encoding), and GraphSynth/MNC demonstrate utility of verifier feedback or constraint encoding paired with generation, improving accuracy on draft configurations. Ops/AIOps benchmarks. OpsEval, LogEval and other AIOps benchmark suites emphasize task realism but often evaluate generation or QA accuracy rather than deterministic enactability. Distinction. Our work ties LLM generation to a deterministic enactment predicate under a preregistered, paired design with full artifacts and exact hashes.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design. The preregistration (c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1; preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest) froze task selection rules, augmentation seeds, model scope (gpt‑5‑mini), paired confirmatory design, primary estimand, analysis plan, retries, and stopping rules. Task set and sampling. Confirmatory N=160 vendor‑neutral tasks: routing ≈64, ACL ≈64, NAT/other ≈32. Tasks were filtered for vendor‑neutral constructs and deterministically augmented using pre‑registered seeds [42,123,999]; selection scripts and hashes are archived. Model and calling semantics. Single hosted model: gpt‑5‑mini; pre‑registered shared_initial_generation semantics (independent_condition_generation=false): one initial generation call per task was shared across conditions (baseline and guarded) as recorded in the provider_call_audit (execution manifest; stage_counts: {"shared_initial_generation":160}). Guarded pipeline. The guarded pipeline applied (in order): canonicalization of the model output, a constraint/validator stage, deterministic simulator enactment, and automatic rollback scoring per the frozen scoring schema. Baseline pipeline. The generation‑only baseline produced the same shared initial candidate; the simulator scored the candidate post‑hoc but the pipeline did not block enactment. Primary outcome. Binary per task: actionable misconfiguration = 1 if the deterministic simulator's scoring predicate flagged a safety violation that would render the configuration unsafe to enact; 0 otherwise. Analysis. Primary estimand: paired difference in actionable proportion (A − C). Pre‑registered analysis: paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for CI; McNemar exact test for the paired binary outcome. Reproducibility. All prompts, seeds, canonicalizers, per‑task scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), provider call logs (execution/provider_calls/*.json), raw model outputs (execution/responses/*), and analysis scripts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes in the execution manifest.
sections.results: Execution and main numerical facts (artifact‑backed). Execution completed per preregistration (execution manifest). Confirmatory pairs completed = 160. Observed counts: baseline actionable = 0/160; guarded actionable = 0/160. Contingency summary: n11 (non‑actionable in both) = 160; n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. Paired difference (A − C) = 0.00. Bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729): [0.00,0.00]. McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.00. Validator and repair activity (artifact‑backed). Per the archived scoring JSONs and provider call logs (paths and SHA‑256 hashes recorded in the execution manifest): (a) blocked_by_validator = 0 (no generated candidate was blocked in a way that later produced an actionable simulator label on the confirmatory set), (b) repairs_attempted = 0, (c) repairs_accepted_and_rescored = 0. The audit also confirms the preregistered shared‑initial generation: no independent alternative generation per condition was produced (provider call audit: stage_counts shows 160 shared initial generations; cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed=false). Artifacts. Representative artifact references: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256: 2445d0f8e9be9cfa34ede1bbe80b82d6f05b51bcafc7c1688d0ed8e1c73d8044), execution/result_schema.json (SHA‑256: 63199db3f7219b969acc5497fae613c8d5df16e081768969f67b7b3024844465), execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256: 28c190a50d06bf19894639f0ed6edc7b2dc3771138bd818422c212c316bf7c5c), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256: 9730d4b08759b4771b5742a7789edf9ff1fc2ed4e8ee69bdc5c783720a2d2ab8) — the execution manifest contains the full per‑file listing and hashes.
sections.discussion: Why the null/degenerate confirmatory outcome? The preregistered target (≥30% relative reduction) assumed a nonzero baseline actionable rate (power plan conservatively used baseline p≈0.30). The observed baseline actionable rate was zero, producing a ceiling effect that makes the preregistered relative‑reduction target unevaluable. Artifact‑backed hypotheses (non‑exclusive): (1) task calibration: the confirmatory set (public/vendor‑neutral examples plus deterministic augmentations) yielded generated candidates that the chosen simulator predicate judged safe under the scoring schema; (2) predicate scope: the deterministic simulator encodes a specific safety predicate (see paragraph below about simulator scoring artifacts and location), which may not capture other operational failure modes; (3) single‑model/single‑prompt scope: results apply to gpt‑5‑mini and the chosen prompts and call budget only. Simulator scoring predicate and where to verify it. We avoid inventing predicate internals in the manuscript text; the canonical scoring schema and the simulator implementation used to produce the per‑task actionable label are archived in the run artifacts. Readers/reviewers can verify the exact checks by inspecting execution/result_schema.json (SHA‑256: 63199db3f7219b969acc5497fae613c8d5df16e081768969f67b7b3024844465), execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256: 28c190a50d06bf19894639f0ed6edc7b2dc3771138bd818422c212c316bf7c5c), and the per‑task scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (many per‑task hashes are recorded in the execution manifest). Construct validity note. Because the claim concerns reduction in 'actionable misconfigurations' as defined by the deterministic scoring predicate, the generality of findings depends on how well the predicate matches an operator's operational safety requirements; we recommend future runs to expand or vary the predicate and include human adjudication where appropriate. Implications for guarded pipelines. A guarded generate→validate→simulate→rollback pipeline can only reduce enactable faults when baseline generation produces enactable faults detectable by the chosen validator/simulator; therefore, empirical benefit depends on both (i) task difficulty and (ii) predicate coverage. Recommendations. For future confirmatory evaluations we (i) calibrate tasks to produce a nonzero baseline actionable rate (adversarial or higher‑difficulty tasks), (ii) evaluate multiple models and prompt variants, (iii) broaden simulator predicates and optionally include human adjudication, and (iv) publish scoring predicates and test suites alongside tasks so the community can iterate reproducibly.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired evaluation of a generate→validate→simulate→rollback pipeline versus generation‑only for LLM‑assisted NetOps using gpt‑5‑mini on 160 confirmatory tasks. Observed outcome: both conditions produced zero actionable misconfigurations under the deterministic simulator (paired difference 0.00, 95% CI [0.00,0.00], McNemar p=1.00). Because baseline=0, the preregistered ≥30% relative‑reduction target is not evaluable (ceiling effect). The run is artifacted and reproducible (execution manifest with SHA‑256 hashes). The null/degenerate outcome highlights the critical importance of (a) task calibration, (b) multi‑model scope, and (c) richer scoring predicates when assessing operational benefits of guarded pipelines; these are concrete directions for follow‑on studies. All artifacts, prompts, per‑task scoring JSONs, provider call logs, and analysis scripts are archived as recorded in the execution manifest for independent re‑scoring or extension.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track).

Models, adapter, and orchestration: primary generative model = gpt‑5‑mini (hosted API). Orchestration and execution used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family under the frozen preregistration c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1. The exact initial master prompt bundle (Master Prompt v1 — Autonomous CNSM 2026 Research Run) and the autonomy boundary are recorded in the preregistration and manifest. Topic constraints: the Research Director selected the broad family “Generative AI and Large Language Models for NetOps” and constrained the scope to operational reliability, validation, and enactability; those constraints are recorded in the preregistration.

Pre‑lock development and autonomy boundary: collaborative pre‑lock infrastructure development and rehearsal occurred and were explicitly excluded from final empirical evidence as required by the track. After the autonomy lock, literature search, research‑gap selection, preregistration, prompt generation, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, autonomous peer review, revision, and manuscript drafting were performed autonomously. No human manually edited technical manuscript content, numerical results, figures, captions, references, or this Disclosure Statement after the autonomy lock.

Preregistration and frozen design: full experimental plan preregistered as c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1 and frozen before execution. Key preregistered elements included: task selection, augmentation seeds, model scope (gpt‑5‑mini), maximum model calls (320), paired confirmatory design (N=160 tasks), primary metric (actionable misconfiguration binary), analysis plan (paired bootstrap 10k, McNemar exact), retry policy, and stopping rules. No post‑hoc changes affecting confirmatory analysis occurred.

Execution artifacts and integrity: all experiment artifacts (preregistration, raw model outputs, provider call logs, canonicalized configurations, per‑task scoring JSONs, deterministic simulator scoring schema, and analysis scripts) are archived. Representative artifact references and SHA‑256 hashes (recorded in the execution manifest) include execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256: 2445d0f8e9be9cfa34ede1bbe80b82d6f05b51bcafc7c1688d0ed8e1c73d8044), execution/result_schema.json (SHA‑256: 63199db3f7219b969acc5497fae613c8d5df16e081768969f67b7b3024844465), execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256: 28c190a50d06bf19894639f0ed6edc7b2dc3771138bd818422c212c316bf7c5c), and the per‑task scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full listing and hashes appear in the execution manifest). These artifacts are the canonical integrity‑verified record for replication and re‑scoring. No invented URLs or repository locations are claimed here beyond the manifest artifact paths and hashes.

Model calls and retries: preregistered maximum model calls = 320; actual model calls used = 160 (one shared initial generation per task). Provider call logs and the call cache are archived; provider_call_audit in the deterministic reconciliation shows stage_counts: {"shared_initial_generation":160} and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed=false. Retries were pre‑registered (up to two) for transient provider failures; none affected confirmatory outcomes.

Human role and limitations: the human Research Director selected the topic family and approved pre‑lock infrastructure development; post‑lock scientific execution and manuscript drafting were autonomous. Precise provider endpoint identifiers and internal provider operational logs are not published here for confidentiality; everything required to reproduce the analysis given the same hosted model API (prompts, seeds, canonicalizers, simulator scoring schema, raw outputs, and per‑artifact SHA‑256) is archived and referenced in the execution manifest. The manifest and artifact SHA‑256 hashes are authoritative for verification of the run.
limitations: Ceiling effect: baseline generation produced zero actionable misconfigurations under the chosen deterministic simulator (baseline=0/160), making the preregistered ≥30% relative‑reduction target unevaluable.
Single‑model scope: results apply to gpt‑5‑mini and the supplied prompts/call budget only; multi‑model generalization is unresolved.

Construct coverage: the deterministic simulator scoring predicate is an abstraction; it may not capture all operational failure modes—inspect execution/result_schema.json and execution/scoring/*.json (SHA‑256 hashes in the execution manifest) to verify predicate details.
Task calibration: confirmatory task set difficulty did not produce a nonzero baseline actionable rate; future confirmatory runs must use adversarial/harder tasks or broaden predicate scope.
No live device enactment: evaluation used deterministic simulator adjudication rather than live production enactment; external validity to production remains limited.
